The Oracle had also answered correctly about that. Croesus's error was not the Oracle. It was the interpretation.

collar_of_njord.name: Sea-Collar of Njörd
collar_of_njord.lore: Njörd ruled the winds and the seas and was responsible for the catch of fish and hunters' luck. He married Skadi, who chose him by his feet — the most beautiful feet among the gods — expecting to have chosen Baldur. They lived six days in her mountains, six by the sea, and both were miserable by turns. Nordic marriage counsellors date their profession's origin to this arrangement.

ring_of_percival.name: Ring of the Pure Knight
ring_of_percival.lore: Percival failed the Grail question because he was too polite to ask what was wrong with the Fisher King. He had been told not to ask too many questions. He followed the instruction and failed. When he returned and asked — Who does the Grail serve? — the king was healed. The lesson of the Grail quest is that courtesy has limits, and sometimes the correct action is to inquire.

ring_of_lancelot.name: Ring of the Fallen Knight
ring_of_lancelot.lore: Lancelot was the greatest knight in the world and destroyed the Round Table by being exactly that. His affair with Guinevere was not a secret he kept — it was a secret everyone kept for him because they needed him too much to confront him. The tower on the ring is the tower of Joyous Gard, where he retreated when his virtue finally failed the test he had spent his life avoiding.

seal_of_agrippa.name: Seal of Agrippa
seal_of_agrippa.lore: Heinrich Cornelius Agrippa published Three Books of Occult Philosophy in 1531, systematizing all of Renaissance magic into a single framework: the elemental world, the celestial world, and the intellectual world. He was accused of heresy, employed by kings, and died in debt. His books were the most widely read magical texts of the 16th century. He himself claimed at the end that they were worthless. He was probably not being entirely honest.

philosophers_ring_legendary.name: Philosopher's Ring of Mastery
philosophers_ring_legendary.lore: The philosopher does not merely think — the philosopher perceives. Socrates described his daimon as a voice that told him what not to do; he considered this the most useful kind of guidance. The ring was found in the ruins of the Academy at Athens, described in a catalogue written three centuries after Plato's death. The description ends mid-sentence. The catalogue's final page is missing.

amulet_of_pythagoras.name: Tetractys Amulet
amulet_of_pythagoras.lore: Pythagoras swore his oaths by the Tetractys — the triangular figure of ten points arranged 1-2-3-4 that represented the musical ratios and the structure of the cosmos. His brotherhood at Croton was vegetarian, banned beans, and believed the soul transmigrated between lives. They were also the first people to prove that the square root of 2 is irrational, a discovery so disturbing that Hippasus, who made it, was allegedly drowned at sea.

ring_of_hypatia.name: Ring of Hypatia
ring_of_hypatia.lore: Hypatia of Alexandria was the foremost mathematician and astronomer of her age, head of the Neoplatonic school, advisor to the prefect Orestes. In 415 CE a Christian mob pulled her from her chariot, dragged her to a church, and killed her. Her father Theon had raised her to be 'a perfect human being.' What destroyed her was not her imperfection. It was that the people around her could not tolerate the example.

ring_of_thunder.name: Ring of Thunder
ring_of_thunder.lore: Forged in the heart of a perpetual thunderstorm by an Aztec storm-caller, this ring hums with suppressed electrical charge. Lightning that strikes the wearer grounds harmlessly through the stone, while the storm energy sharpens the intellect to razor clarity.

amulet_of_the_titan.name: Amulet of the Titan
amulet_of_the_titan.lore: Cast from ore pulled from the bones of fallen Titans by Hephaestus as a jest, this amulet transfers a sliver of Titanic strength to the wearer. Those with the constitution to bear it find themselves capable of feats of impossible might.

ring_of_the_deep.name: Ring of the Deep
ring_of_the_deep.lore: Carved from a bioluminescent crystal found only at extreme ocean depth, this ring adapts the wearer's constitution to the crushing cold of the abyss. Divers of the Phoenician coast traded entire fortunes for such rings, which allowed descent to waters where no natural body could survive.

amulet_of_insight.name: Amulet of Insight
amulet_of_insight.lore: Handed down through thirty-six generations of oracle-priests at Delphi, this focus crystal was used to receive the god's voice without distortion. The priests believed wisdom was not intelligence but receptivity — and this amulet sharpens that receptivity to inhuman degree.

ring_of_the_assassin.name: Ring of the Assassin
ring_of_the_assassin.lore: The signet of the Hashshashin grandmaster, recovered after the sack of Alamut. The ring's stone refracts light around the wearer with unsettling precision. Paired with the supernatural quickness it grants, its bearer becomes effectively impossible to track in dim light.

amulet_of_fortitude.name: Amulet of Fortitude
amulet_of_fortitude.lore: A gift from Asclepius to a mortal champion whose constitution had been ravaged by poison. The carved serpent at its centre channels a fraction of divine healing energy into the wearer continuously. Wounds knit, poisons fade, and exhaustion retreats in its presence.

ring_of_far_sight.name: Ring of Far Sight
ring_of_far_sight.lore: Fashioned by the eagle-eyed sentinels of the Watchtower of Rhodes, worn by scouts who needed to perceive threats at inhuman range. The iris of its gem dilates and contracts like an eye, and something in that motion transmits itself to the wearer — both sight and instinct are magnified.

amulet_of_the_archmage.name: Amulet of the Archmage
amulet_of_the_archmage.lore: The ceremonial amulet of the Dean of the Arcane Faculty — a position first held by Thales, who wore it when demonstrating that fire could not harm a mind that understood its nature. Since then it has passed through the hands of thirty-seven archmages, each adding a layer of heat-resistant enchantment.

ring_of_displacement.name: Ring of Displacement
ring_of_displacement.lore: The gem in this ring is a shard of a displacer beast's crystallized nervous tissue — the organ responsible for the beast's light-bending ability. It projects a constant false image approximately one step from the wearer's true position, causing every attack to land on air.

amulet_of_protection.name: Amulet of Protection
amulet_of_protection.lore: Blessed by the last high priest of Esagila, the great ziggurat of Babylon, this amulet projects an invisible ward that absorbs and dissipates magical energy before it can take hold. Even the most precisely aimed enchantments fray and fail against its steady resistance.

sphinx_crown.name: Sphinx's Crown
sphinx_crown.lore: The crown of the Sphinx, imbued with millennia of accumulated riddle-wisdom. Wearing it sharpens the mind and extends the time available for all mental challenges.

sailors_amulet.name: Sailor's Amulet
sailors_amulet.lore: Carved from the wood of a ship that survived Charybdis, this amulet carries the protection of calm water. The wearer reads the currents of danger before they arrive.

anubis_scales.name: Anubis's Scales
anubis_scales.lore: A miniature of the scales Anubis uses to weigh hearts against the feather of Ma'at. Wearing them steadies the pulse and hardens the bearer against the drain of undead.

ring_of_iron_grip.name: Ring of Iron Grip
ring_of_iron_grip.lore: Crushed from a finger of Ravana himself, this ring channels the demon king's immense physical power into whoever wears it. The grip becomes unbreakable.

obsidian_talisman.name: Obsidian Talisman
obsidian_talisman.lore: Carved from sacrificial obsidian used in Xibalba, the Mayan underworld. It grants the wearer sight in magical darkness and resistance to fear effects from undead.

ariadnes_thread.name: Ariadne's Thread
ariadnes_thread.lore: Ariadne gave this thread to Theseus so he could find his way out of the Labyrinth. The thread remembers every path it has traveled and guides its bearer toward the exit. In the myth, Theseus abandoned Ariadne on Naxos — but the thread remained faithful.

eponas_charm.name: Epona's Charm
eponas_charm.lore: Epona was the Celtic goddess of horses, travelers, and safe journeys. Her charm ensures the traveler always arrives in safe harbor — never in a dead end, never in an ambush. The Romans adopted her worship, unique among Gaulish deities.

anansis_thread.name: Anansi's Thread
anansis_thread.lore: Anansi the spider-god of the Akan people earned all the stories in the world by outwitting the sky-god Nyame. His thread connects all knowledge — what you learn once, you never lose. The Ashanti say that every story belongs to Anansi.

rope_of_izanagi.name: Rope of Izanagi
rope_of_izanagi.lore: When Izanagi fled the underworld of Yomi, he sealed the entrance with a great boulder and a sacred rope. The rope divides the world of the living from the dead. Its bearer can feel the boundary thinning — every trap, every hidden passage, every secret door reveals itself to one who knows where life ends and death begins.

silverlight_pendant.name: Silverlight Pendant
silverlight_pendant.lore: A small silver pendant on a fine chain. The metal is warm to the touch, as though someone held it very recently. The name 'ELARA' is engraved on the back in a child's unsteady hand.

saints_reliquary.name: Saint's Reliquary
saints_reliquary.lore: A silver reliquary containing the fingerbone of a saint, set in gold. The monk who carried it crawled through the dungeon on his hands and knees to keep it safe. It radiates a quiet warmth.

officers_signet.name: Officer's Signet
officers_signet.lore: A solid gold signet ring bearing the crest of the Legion. Officer-grade — only issued to those who have earned command. The previous owner pulled it off his own finger and said he didn't deserve it.

prophets_amulet.name: Prophet's Amulet
prophets_amulet.lore: An amulet worn by a dying prophet who spent his last years carving warnings into stone tablets. It pulses with accumulated foresight — visions of the Destroyer, the Seven Seals, and the final battle. The clarity it grants is almost painful.

aesops_quill.name: Aesop's Quill
aesops_quill.lore: Aesop was a slave in ancient Greece who earned his freedom through storytelling. His fables — The Tortoise and the Hare, The Boy Who Cried Wolf, The Fox and the Grapes — taught moral wisdom through animals. This quill-shaped ring carries that legacy: the wisdom to see truth in simple things. +2 WIS.

lyre_of_orpheus.name: Lyre of Orpheus
lyre_of_orpheus.lore: Orpheus, son of Apollo, played music so beautiful that rocks wept, rivers paused, and the trees leaned in to listen. He descended into Hades to retrieve his beloved Eurydice, charming Cerberus and Persephone with his song. He failed only because he looked back. This tiny lyre amulet hums with that impossible music — while you wear it, no enchantment of sleep can reach you. You will never lose consciousness against your will.

tablet_of_gilgamesh.name: Tablet of Gilgamesh
tablet_of_gilgamesh.lore: The Epic of Gilgamesh is the oldest known work of literature — a Sumerian king's quest for immortality, written on clay tablets four thousand years ago. Gilgamesh was two-thirds god and one-third man, and his story teaches that true immortality lies not in living forever, but in the deeds that outlive you. This ring carries a fragment of that first epic — knowledge and endurance in equal measure. +1 INT, +1 CON.

scales_of_maat.name: Scales of Ma'at
scales_of_maat.lore: In the Egyptian Hall of Two Truths, the heart of the dead was weighed against the feather of Ma'at, goddess of truth and cosmic order. If the heart was lighter than the feather — free of sin — the soul passed into the Field of Reeds. If heavier, the demon Ammit devoured it. These tiny scales whisper of that judgment: see clearly, judge wisely. +1 WIS, +1 PER.

tablet_of_hammurabi.name: Tablet of Hammurabi
tablet_of_hammurabi.lore: Hammurabi, King of Babylon, created the first comprehensive written law code around 1750 BC — 282 laws carved in stone, establishing the revolutionary principle that justice should be written, public, and consistent rather than arbitrary. 'An eye for an eye' comes from his code. This tablet-shaped amulet carries the weight of that first attempt to replace chaos with order. +2 INT.

torc_of_boudicca.name: Torc of Boudicca
torc_of_boudicca.lore: The golden torc of Boudicca, queen of the Iceni, who burned Londinium and Camulodunum to the ground rather than submit to Rome. Her fury was greatest when surrounded — the more enemies, the fiercer she fought. The torc channels that defiance. When hemmed in on all sides, the wearer becomes harder to hit, as though Boudicca herself stands beside them.

rands_heart.name: Rand's Heart
rands_heart.lore: A simple silver locket on a leather thong. It is infused with the power of a lover's promise. He knew he could not always be by Robyn's side, but he swore to protect her, always.

dreamspun_sketchbook.name: Dreamspun Sketchbook
dreamspun_sketchbook.lore: A young lady's sketchbook. It's full of whimsical drawings. She used this sketchbook to bring her dreams to life. The pages shimmer with magical energy.

charmander_stuffie.name: Charmander Stuffie
charmander_stuffie.lore: A child's favorite toy and oldest friend. It looks like a small orange dragon with a burning ember on the tip of its tail. The love shown to this toy has imbued it with a shimmering magical power that protects and strengthens the bearer.

jade_cicada.name: Jade Cicada
jade_cicada.lore: Placed on the tongues of the dead during the Han Dynasty to ensure resurrection. The cicada burrows into the earth and emerges reborn — the Chinese symbol of immortality. This one was never buried. It clings to life with an insect's tenacity: once per floor, when a blow would kill its wearer, the cicada intervenes. The wearer survives with a single breath left. The jade cracks — but holds.

seal_of_solomon.name: Seal of Solomon
seal_of_solomon.lore: The ring given to Solomon by the Archangel Michael, engraved with the true name of God. With it Solomon commanded demons to build the First Temple and bound Asmodeus in a jar of brass. Its power compels obedience — nearby enemies may find themselves frozen in place, unable to act, their will subverted by a force older than anger.

kavacha_kundala.name: Kavacha and Kundala
kavacha_kundala.lore: Karna was born wearing them — gifts of Surya the Sun, fused to his skin so that no weapon could harm him while he wore them. Indra came to him as a beggar and asked for them as alms; Karna cut them off and gave them, because a Brahmin's request cannot be refused. He died on the eighteenth day of Kurukshetra. From the Mahabharata, Vana Parva.

circes_wand.name: Circe's Wand
circes_wand.lore: Circe's wand from her hall on Aeaea. She used it on Odysseus's crew and they became swine — heads and bristles and grunts, but their minds knew themselves the whole time. Hermes gave Odysseus the herb moly to resist her; she gave up after the swine-spell failed and welcomed him. From the Odyssey, Book X.

indras_vajra.name: Indra's Vajra
indras_vajra.lore: The thunderbolt of Indra, made by Tvastr the divine craftsman from the bones of the sage Dadhichi, who gave his body for it. Indra struck Vritra the world-drought serpent with this and freed the seven rivers. From the Rigveda, Book I. It is not lightning — it is the weapon that lightning was a memory of.

book_of_thoth.name: Book of Thoth
book_of_thoth.lore: The book of Thoth, Egyptian god of writing. Pharaoh Neferkaptah stole it from its serpent guardian in the Nile and learned the speech of the birds and the fish and the dead; his family drowned for his audacity, and the book was buried with him. Reading it identifies what was hidden. From the Setna cycle.

sefer_yetzirah.name: Sefer Yetzirah (The Book of Formation)
sefer_yetzirah.lore: The Book of Formation. Attributed to Abraham; the oldest extant Jewish mystical text. It teaches the twenty-two letters of the Hebrew alphabet and the ten sefirot, and how the world was spoken into being. The Maharal of Prague used a copy in the sixteenth century to shape a golem of clay; the golem walked the streets of the Jewish quarter until the Maharal removed the Name from its forehead.

picatrix.name: Picatrix
picatrix.lore: Picatrix — Ghayat al-Hakim, the Aim of the Sage. Composed in tenth-century al-Andalus, translated to Latin under Alfonso X, and read across Europe for the next four centuries. It teaches talismanic magic, planetary hours, and how to summon fire by naming a planet's degree of ascension. Dee owned a copy. Ficino read it carefully and pretended he hadn't.

lemegeton.name: Lemegeton (The Lesser Key of Solomon)
lemegeton.lore: The Lemegeton. Five books bound as one; the first, the Ars Goetia, lists the seventy-two demons King Solomon bound to his service. Each demon has a sigil, a number of legions, and a particular use — Bael teaches invisibility, Asmodeus answers questions truthfully, Vassago finds lost things. Crowley translated it in 1904. Read it carefully.
